| 2026-05-09 (late evening +1, build pipeline) | DOCX styling via `--reference-doc` wired; T&F generic Word template staged at `common/reference.docx`; assembled markdown now published alongside `.docx`/`.pdf` | Two small but-load-bearing conventions added on top of the build pipeline. **(1) `--reference-doc` plumbing.** Pandoc reads named styles, page geometry, margins, and fonts from a reference Word document; body content still comes from markdown. Wired into `Builder#render_docx` with the precedence chain `<paper-dir>/reference.docx` → `common/reference.docx` → none (pandoc defaults), mirroring the existing CSL-fallback shape. The build prints `(docx styled from <path>)` after success so the styling source is never silent. T&F's generic Word template (`TF_Template_Word_Windows_2016.dotx`, downloaded from <https://authstaging.wpengine.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/TF_Template_Word_Windows_2016.zip> per the link surfaced from the formatting-and-templates page in the *Inquiry* submission-guidelines PDF) is staged at `common/reference.docx`; the original `.dotx` and `.zip` archived untouched at `common/vendor/` for provenance. With this template applied, the build's DOCX picks up T&F's page geometry (A4 portrait, 25mm top/bottom × 30mm left/right margins), Times New Roman as the default body font, and en-GB locale — verified by extracting `document.xml` and `styles.xml` from the output. Of pandoc's named styles, three map cleanly by name (`Heading 1`/`Heading 2` → T&F's `heading 1`/`heading 2`; `Abstract` → `Abstract`; would also map `Keywords`, `Footnote Text`, `Footnote Reference`, `Endnote Text`, `Endnote Reference` if used). Four don't auto-map: pandoc's `Title` vs T&F's `Article title`; `Author` vs `Author names`; `Block Text` (blockquotes ≥50 w) vs `Displayed quotation`; `Bibliography` vs `References`. Those still render — they just use Word's default styles rather than T&F house styling. To wire them up, edit `common/reference.docx` in Word and add the pandoc-name as an alias on the corresponding T&F style; the README documents the table. T&F provides a single generic Word template across its journal portfolio (no Inquiry-specific variant; verified). **(2) Assembled markdown published.** The DOCX-intent intermediate (`.build/<stem>/<stem>.md`) is now also published to `<paper-dir>/<stem>.md` alongside the `.docx` and `.pdf`. Rationale: for a paper assembled from a dozen segments, the concatenated markdown is the most readable / greppable / shareable form of the "final" paper — useful for self-review, for diff against prior builds, for sharing with colleagues, and for any future agent that wants to see the whole prose at once without flipping through `src/*.md` segments or extracting prose from a Word file. The published copy carries an HTML banner inserted just after the YAML frontmatter (`<!-- Built by bin/build from src/*.md per OUT.<stem>.md. Source-of-truth lives in src/; edits to this file are overwritten on the next build. -->`) so a curious reader / agent immediately sees this is a build output and doesn't try to edit it. The PDF-intent intermediate (`.build/<stem>/<stem>.pdf-preview.md`) stays in `.build/` — it differs from the DOCX intermediate only in the stripped `keywords:` field, and one published copy is enough. README + script-header doc updated with the new output layout. |
| 2026-05-09 (late evening, build pipeline) | Three real issues in `bin/build` + `bin/refs` surfaced by paper-3 sanity test, all fixed | Sanity-tested the freshly-wired build pipeline against the 12-segment paper-3 stub; surfaced three issues the minimum-viable port had missed and fixed them in this session. **(1) `bin/refs` CitationScanner only matched LaTeX `\cite{}` — pandoc-native `[@key]` was invisible.** The original `CITE_RE` only caught natbib commands, so all 14 `[@key]` / bare `@key` citations the drafter sprinkled in stub prose produced an *empty* emitted bib and pandoc-citeproc reported every key as "not found". Added `PANDOC_CITE_RE = /(?<![[:alnum:]_\\])@([[:alnum:]_][[:alnum:]_:.\#$%&+?<>~\/-]*)/` matching the pandoc citation-key spec; both regexes feed `call_sites` so `emit` / `cited` / `lint` all see both syntaxes. Negative lookbehind blocks email-address (`user@host`) and escape-form (`\@key`) false matches; trailing-punctuation post-strip drops sentence-end periods/commas from keys. Same bug exists in `~/src/neurips/bin/refs` (the upstream copy, forked into this repo on 2026-05-09 — not a symlink); flagged for parallel fix at Joseph's discretion. While there: also added HTML-comment stripping in CitationScanner (`<!--…-->` blanked to whitespace before scanning, line numbers preserved) — pandoc itself ignores comment content, so literal `[@key]` / `\cite{key}` examples in `src/references.md`'s explanatory comment were producing a phantom `key` entry in lint output. Verified post-fix: paper 3 picks up 14 keys (vs 0 before); the only "missing" report is the intentional `noop-tf-ai-policy-2026` placeholder. **(2) lualatex `\xmpquote` fatal on PDF-preview keywords had not actually been suppressed.** The pre-existing `--metadata=keywords:` CLI override in `render_pdf_preview` was a hopeful stopgap that doesn't work — pandoc accepts the override but the YAML keywords list still flows through the LaTeX template's `$for(keywords)$` loop into hyperxmp's `\xmpquote{...}` macro, fatalling on the first run. Real fix: factor `assemble_markdown` to write *two* intermediate markdowns — `<stem>.md` (full frontmatter, for DOCX) and `<stem>.pdf-preview.md` (`keywords:` field omitted at YAML-assembly time, for PDF). Body assembly happens once; only the frontmatter differs. The CLI hack is removed. Keywords still flow into the DOCX through its own intermediate. **(3) Abstract double-rendered between meta.md (YAML) and `src/00-abstract.md` (concatenated body row).** New convention: any manifest row with slug `abstract` is *lifted* — its file content becomes the YAML `abstract:` field (overriding meta.md's body) and the row is skipped from body concatenation. The lifting routine drops a leading H1 and italic-only paragraphs (drafter notes like `*Drafted last per protocol.*`) so the source file can carry structural and workflow markers without polluting the metadata. Citations inside the abstract (`[-@nagel-1974-bat]` etc.) are processed by pandoc citeproc when rendered from a metadata field, so the abstract's bibliography integrates with the rest of the paper. Honours Joseph's "abstract drafted last as a separate file" workflow without double-rendering against meta.md's placeholder; meta.md body is preserved as fallback for paper-dirs that don't carry an abstract row. **Verified post-fix:** `bin/build 03-inquiry-ai-agents inquiry-ai-agents-2026` produces `.docx` (18 KB) and `.pdf` (64 KB) cleanly; abstract appears exactly once in both; bibliography has 13 entries with Chicago author-date forms ("Nagel (1974)", "Cappelen (2018)", "Korsgaard 1996, 2009", etc.); en-dashes / smart quotes / footnotes / blockquotes all preserved. Updated `bin/build.README.md` with the abstract-lifting convention and the two-intermediate model so the next agent finds these explicit rather than tribal. |
